## Purpose and Entry Points
Archinstall is a Python-based guided and automated Arch Linux installer, also exposed as a library for scripted installation and in-target system management. CLI/module startup is `archinstall/__main__.py` and `archinstall/main.py`; argument parsing and script selection are centralized in `archinstall/lib/args.py`. The default execution mode is the guided installer at `archinstall/scripts/guided.py`; alternative installation scripts include `archinstall/scripts/minimal.py` and `archinstall/scripts/only_hd.py`.

## Orchestration and Installation Boundary
The guided flow collects an installation configuration, validates choices through menus, then drives the installer engine. `archinstall/lib/global_menu.py` coordinates the major selectable domains, while `archinstall/lib/configuration.py` loads, saves, and interprets declarative configuration and credentials. `archinstall/lib/installer.py` is the main imperative boundary that applies the plan to the target system. It runs with system-level privileges, changing real disks and the mounted target filesystem rather than serving a remote application.

## Interactive TUI and Localization
Terminal interaction is separated into reusable menu infrastructure and domain menus. Core menu abstractions are in `archinstall/lib/menu/abstract_menu.py` and `archinstall/tui/components.py`; installation domains expose menus such as `archinstall/lib/disk/disk_menu.py` and `archinstall/lib/network/network_menu.py`. Translation lookup is handled by `archinstall/lib/translationhandler.py`, backed by compiled and source gettext catalogs under `archinstall/locales/`.

## Storage, Filesystems, and Encryption
Disk selection and partitioning form a high-risk subsystem: hardware/device discovery, partition layouts, filesystem creation/mounting, and target preparation are divided across `archinstall/lib/disk/device_handler.py`, `archinstall/lib/disk/filesystem.py`, and `archinstall/lib/disk/partitioning_menu.py`. Encryption and volume-management choices are represented and applied through `archinstall/lib/disk/luks.py`, `archinstall/lib/disk/lvm.py`, and `archinstall/lib/disk/encryption_menu.py`. This layer interfaces with local block devices and Linux storage tooling, including the `parted` API (typing stub at `stubs/parted/__init__.pyi`).

## Base-System Provisioning and Boot
After storage is prepared and mounted, the installer provisions Arch packages and bootability. Pacman configuration and package operations are encapsulated in `archinstall/lib/pacman/config.py` and `archinstall/lib/pacman/pacman.py`; broader package selection is in `archinstall/lib/packages/packages.py`. Bootloader selection/configuration is isolated in `archinstall/lib/bootloader/bootloader_menu.py` and `archinstall/lib/boot.py`. These stages depend on Arch Linux repositories, package mirrors, `pacman`, and the target system’s firmware/boot environment.

## Network, Mirrors, and System Identity
Network connectivity is both an installer prerequisite and a configured target concern. Wireless/network operations live in `archinstall/lib/network/network_handler.py` and `archinstall/lib/network/wifi_handler.py`, with `wpa_supplicant` integration in `archinstall/lib/network/wpa_supplicant.py`. Mirror selection and mirrorlist handling are separated in `archinstall/lib/mirror/mirror_handler.py`. Locale, users, authentication, and host/system settings are collected through `archinstall/lib/locale/locale_menu.py`, `archinstall/lib/user/user_menu.py`, and `archinstall/lib/authentication/authentication_handler.py`.

## Profiles, Applications, and Extensibility
Profiles layer optional system roles over the base installation. Profile discovery and selection are in `archinstall/lib/profile/profiles_handler.py`; common role definitions are `archinstall/default_profiles/desktop.py`, `archinstall/default_profiles/server.py`, and `archinstall/default_profiles/minimal.py`. Desktop and server implementations install role-specific packages/services from `archinstall/default_profiles/desktops/` and `archinstall/default_profiles/servers/`. Post-base optional applications are managed by `archinstall/lib/applications/application_handler.py`. Plugins are a separate extension boundary at `archinstall/lib/plugins.py`, allowing customization without modifying the principal installer flow.
